grades.missing: No chunk says the organisation's assumptions generate bottleneck queues, reward quality compromises or create single-point failures. The chunks carry only organisational weaknesses and latent conditions as causes of error, and a Resource Topology aimed at 100% utilisation.

No chunk names the 'nobody is idle' rule splitting developers across two or three squads as the primary driver of delivery collapse. [3] describes 100% utilisation and [4] describes personal overload from taking on many tasks.
No chunk says queue and lead times rise exponentially as utilisation nears 100%. [6] carries only the formula Cycle Time = WIP / Throughput.

No chunk links multi-squad assignment to inflated WIP, and none names 'massive context-switching overhead'. The chunks say only that taking on many tasks overloads people and that multitasking does not work.
No chunk says communication overhead grows non-linearly with team interdependencies. [8] models communication overhead and peak team size against team size, not interdependencies.

No chunk carries the case figures (60 engineers, 9 squads), the claim that being split across squads causes the harm, or the handover friction and stalled velocity. The chunks carry only that focus improves delivery.
No chunk says 100% busy people inevitably yield 0% flow efficiency. [9] says only that everyone can be busy while work gets done more slowly.

No chunk carries the specific sacrifices (skipped automated testing, cut code reviews, architectural shortcuts) or says thoroughness is sacrificed 'systematically' when pay is tied to output volume. [13] says money tied to goals raises commitment and that quantity can crowd out quality; [14] shows quality losing to job preservation.

No chunk links the throughput incentive to a surge in technical debt, or carries the surge in production defects. [15] says only that shortcuts create technical debt that may cause bigger problems later.

No chunk says churn is driven by bugs, or that engineering is explicitly incentivised to generate bugs. [16] lists productivity-only bonuses as a weakness; [13] and [14] show quantity or job preservation winning over quality.

No chunk calls a PIP for the developer a 'critical organisational mistake'. The chunks do not say the merge was an honest error; they say to stop blaming and retraining people for honest errors, and that changing personnel gives a false impression the problem is solved.
No chunk carries the case-specific pathogens (unclear rollback procedures, missing automated integration tests, fatigue).
No chunk mentions code generation. [28] says only that AI boosts efficiency on routine 'Doing' tasks.

No chunk says AI cannot solve a structural queueing or alignment problem. [30] says AI makes broader skills and work mandates easier.
No chunk calls for dedicated, stable teams aligned to product capabilities, or carries the 60-engineer restructure. The chunks carry WIP limits and cross-functional teams that remove dependencies.
No chunk names multi-squad context-switching as the single greatest bottleneck.

No chunk names task-switching as the bottleneck, or says target-setting, process changes or AI tools will fail until it clears. The chunks carry only the general rule that improving anything other than the bottleneck is an illusion.
No chunk says single-squad dedication 'instantly' reduces WIP or restores 'predictable flow'. [36] says that working one task at a time keeps a person responsive and their status visible.
No chunk carries Defect Escape Rate, shared customer outcomes co-owned by Product, Marketing and Engineering, or replacing sprint velocity targets.
No chunk carries point inflation, quality cutting as an effect of the incentive, or the sequencing ('once WIP is capped').
No chunk says 'automated' deployment guardrails or a shift in investment. The chunks carry quality gates, strengthening controls and safeguards, and defence in depth in general.
No chunk links reporting to unclogging the workflow. The chunks carry a reporting culture and a just culture only as safety and learning concerns.

No chunk names automated regression test generation, pull-request verification or deployment pipeline checks, or says to move away from general code generation. [29] says only to aim AI at the main bottleneck rather than a generic 'adopt AI'.
